youtube.title: What if you were a plague doctor in 1656?
youtube.description:
Rome, 1656: the plague is back and the city pays you to walk where nobody else will – beak mask, herbs, waxed coat and a stick. 🕯️ But did the famous mask actually protect plague doctors?
Would you take this job? A) Yes, someone has to B) Only with the coat C) Never – Comment A, B or C 👇
Sources: National Geographic (Why plague doctors wore those strange beaked masks), British Museum ("Doctor Schnabel von Rom", Paulus Fürst, 1656), University of Münster (plague in Rome 1656/57), Wikipedia (Naples Plague 1656 – death estimates range from about a third to over half of the city). The costume is often credited to Charles de Lorme (1619), but historians debate how widely it was really worn.
